text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds end near the highs after a day of mixed German economic data. The market had feared GDP would be higher than it was. Stronger European markets were also supportive. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 97.28, up 0.06 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts trundled higher to close in positive territory after suffering small losses in mid-session following an upbeat CBI retail survey, buoyed by unchanged interest rates. All eyes are on Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls figure, expected to be robust. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-01/32, up 05/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French interest rate futures rallied late on, wiping out earlier losses, as the franc gained ground against the mark. The franc climbed to a high of 3.4224 at 1455 GMT after slipping overnight below its old exchange rate mechanism floor. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 123.48, up 0.22 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures surged in late trading, breaking through resistance at 115.15, and closed sharply higher on hopes of a new Bank of Italy discount rate cut and a firmer lira against the mark. A good tone in bunds was also underpinning sentiment. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 115.47, up 0.76 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were off but well above the day's lows by midday as prices pared losses after the market played down the likelihood of a 50 basis point rate hike by the Federal Reserve in September. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-05/32, down 11/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.13 percent.

JAPAN - Key December 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended lower, hurt by a steady advance in Tokyo share prices in the afternoon. Another factor behind the fall was two- to four-year interest rate swap payments by major Japanese banks, traders said. The payment was mainly aimed at taking profits from the recent fall in swap rates. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 120.64, up 0.01 from the settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market business was much slower but the morning session still managed to produce a handful of notable transactions. Baden-Wuerttemberg L-Finance led the way with a 750 million mark five-year offering. Joint lead managers Goldman Sachs International and SBC Warburg gave the 5.25 percent notes a 99.507 reoffer price for a spread of 22 basis points over German government paper.
